purpose: Individual reconciliation of E3/E5 and dependent principle findings. E2/positive Sovereignty contradictions in this batch are also corrected; unchanged E1/E4/Locality findings are not independently re-certified.

applications.name: restic
E3: Full-data reading is opt-in and TAR carries more metadata than ZIP, but retained source does not demonstrate decrypting a preserved repository, restoring the declared filesystem records, or comparing ownership, links, ACLs and xattrs with a baseline. These positive implementation findings are not a complete recovery record.
E5: The inspected forget command reports retention selections and gates snapshot removal on dry-run; its prune call propagates dry-run, and the prune implementation returns before mutation in that mode. These establish useful retention safeguards, not the whole assessed operation surface: restore overwrite/delete, key-management authorization and recovery from interrupted mutations remain insufficiently evidenced.
applications.remaining: A synthetic encrypted repository and expected file/metadata manifest, a matched restore report using preserved recovery material, and records for restore overwrite/delete, key changes and interrupted pruning remain missing. TAR/ZIP source differences and optional full-data checking are already answered; do not reopen those documentation questions.
applications.next: Obtain an upstream or independent version-matched synthetic recovery evidence packet: repository/configuration, non-secret test credentials, baseline manifest, commands and before/after output. Independently compare recovered bytes, paths, links and metadata using existing tools; no local restic installation is required if the restore was reproducibly run elsewhere.
longevity: E3 remains Not Verified for restic's existing essential-record scope. Documented/exported structure does not establish a baseline-matched clean recovery. The previous positive Longevity finding is withdrawn to Not assessed, not a finding of failure.

applications.name: BorgBackup
E3: The development source writes interpretable TAR fields plus Borg-specific metadata; ordinary TAR readers do not automatically interpret that extension. No preserved encrypted repository, compatible-key recovery or baseline-matched extraction was exercised. Results cannot be transferred to Borg 1.x or a released Borg 2 binary merely because their documentation looks similar.
E5: The inspected development branch supplies a repair warning/typed acknowledgement, soft-delete/undelete and compaction dry-run. Normal compaction closes the soft-delete window. These control paths are concrete evidence, but extraction overwrite, credential handling and an observed delete/undelete/compact recovery sequence are not sufficiently covered for the existing backup scope.
applications.remaining: A declared released version or exact development build, a populated synthetic repository with baseline metadata and preserved recovery material, compatible restore evidence, and before/after delete/undelete/compact, repair and extraction-overwrite records remain missing. Existing source conclusions are limited to the pinned development tree.
applications.next: Request a reproducible packet for the exact assessed commit or explicitly reassess a released version. Use a disposable synthetic repository and expected manifest, with delete/undelete output before compaction and separately backed-up post-compaction evidence. Independent TAR/manifest inspection can happen here without installing Borg.

applications.name: Anki
E3: Reinspection reproduces integrity ok and the one-card/one-note join and sound-name mapping in the retained legacy APKG. Its mapped media member is only four bytes, not proof of usable audio. Modern package decoding, deck/options and scheduling semantics, complete media and a meaningful collection restore are not covered by this historical fixture.
E5: Pinned desktop source provides full-sync direction/cancel choices, confirmation paths and a backup call before full download. The undo manager keeps bounded in-memory operations and can clear them. These answer control-path questions but do not establish complete media-inclusive recovery, normal sync conflict handling or restoration after collection-wide destructive actions in the declared learning workflow.
applications.remaining: A modern synthetic collection package with expected notes/cards, deck/options, scheduling and genuine media, independent decoding/comparison, and full-sync/deletion/recovery output remain missing. Legacy readability, full-sync confirmation/backup calls and bounded undo are already resolved; their coverage limits are explicit.
applications.next: Obtain a current-version APKG/COLPKG test export and expected semantic manifest from upstream fixtures or an external assessor. Independently decode and compare it here, keeping notes, cards, options and scheduling together. A recorded restore/sync exercise elsewhere can supply behavior evidence without a local Anki installation.
applications.exit: The prior E2 Pass rested on a generic documentation lead. The retained legacy fixture establishes readable records, not a usable alternative study workflow preserving the stated scheduling/deck/media meaning. E2 is withdrawn to Not Verified pending an independent conversion and comparison.

findings.text: The full-sync conflict dialog offers upload, download and cancellation with cancellation as that dialog's default. Dedicated full-upload/full-download confirmation paths also exist; the full-download worker calls create_backup_now before closing for replacement. This proves code paths, not a successful or media-complete backup.

The undo manager stores a bounded in-memory queue, truncates old steps and clears undo/redo when a step begins without an undoable operation. Undo therefore is not a durable or universal recovery archive.

applications.name: Joplin
E3: JEX/raw implementation and inspected import assertions explain serialized items, resource copying, new IDs and rewritten links, but no populated 200-note profile was independently reconstructed. Complete notebook/tag/link/resource relationships and the declared encrypted/offline-conflict recovery scenario remain unverified; package structure alone is not meaningful restoration.
E5: Pinned source adds concrete trash controls: desktop empty-trash asks for confirmation before calling deletion; restore clears deletion state with explicit missing-parent handling; automatic deletion is setting-gated, uses a configured age and logs selected items. These are positive controls, not a complete account of sync conflicts, encryption changes, transmission or recovery after permanent deletion.
applications.remaining: A populated JEX/raw export with expected notebook/tag/link/resource relationships, independent reconstruction and encrypted/offline-conflict recovery records remain missing. For E5, record sync conflicts, encryption transitions and recovery boundaries after permanent deletion. Trash confirmation, missing-parent restore handling and setting-gated automatic deletion are now answered in source.
applications.next: Acquire a synthetic JEX/raw export plus expected relationship and resource hashes; reconstruct it with archive/text/SQLite tools already available. findings.text: Desktop empty-trash displays a permanent-deletion confirmation and calls the trash deletion service only when accepted. The service invokes note/folder deletion; this is not evidence that history or synchronized copies can recover a permanent deletion.

Trash restoration clears deleted_time and restores the parent when available. Missing/deleted parents use either an explicitly requested restore folder or an empty parent ID, unless a target folder is supplied; folder restoration recurses into children.

Automatic trash deletion exits when its enable setting is false, reads an age setting, logs selected items and excludes share-read-only items. It auto-deletes folders only when empty. Inspected setup schedules periodic processing; default setting values and cross-device consequences were not established here.

Preparing queries against DDL cannot demonstrate recovered research records, attachment bytes, annotation meaning or document-citation mappings. A populated library/storage backup and its expected relations remain necessary.
E5: Pinned source stages trash/restore undo information and implements restoring selected records and children. Manual empty-trash confirms the irreversible action and then clears undo history. A separate timer can empty aged trash according to a preference, so manual confirmation is not universal. Merge, synchronization and backup-replacement control/recourse remain insufficiently covered.
applications.remaining: A populated synthetic library plus stored/linked attachments and a citation-bearing document, expected collection/tag/relation/annotation mappings and an independent recovery comparison remain missing. E5 still needs merge, synchronization and backup-replacement evidence, including automatic-trash preference/retention behavior; source trash/restore/manual-purge boundaries are answered.
applications.next: Use a sanitized synthetic zotero.sqlite, storage directory, any linked-file dependencies and a citation-bearing sample document with an expected mapping manifest. Inspect them with SQLite/archive tools and obtain version-matched merge/sync/backup-restoration observations from upstream or another assessor without installing Zotero locally.

findings.text: The pinned trash path stages undo data before setting deletion state. Selected-item restoration runs transactionally, clears deletion state and includes applicable child notes/attachments or subcollections. This is source evidence of intended recovery paths, not a populated-library recovery run.

locators: // Record undo data before modifying state

findings.text: Manual empty-trash asks for confirmation including an irreversible-action message, erases deleted objects and clears undo history. Separately, the item service can purge aged trash from an idle timer using a preference; the manual dialog must not be generalized to all purges or to an observed default retention value.

supporting_evidence.text: The pinned item service stages undo information before changing an item's trash state. Its idle observer separately reads trashAutoEmptyDays and can call emptyTrash for aged items; a false/zero preference stops that observer path. This establishes source-level controls, not the default retention value, guaranteed audit-log persistence or successful recovery after erasure.
